correctness.rationale: The published theorem supplies the universal four-state upper bound 5. A direct ternary witness rejects every word shorter than 5 and accepts abbac. For the binary upper bound, all four direction splits are exhausted. Each input letter has all 5^4 possible partial direction-compatible state maps; all relevant end-marker returns, symmetry types of the initial entrance, and singleton final states are covered. The search intentionally decouples the initial entrance from later left-endmarker behavior, producing a superset of actual automata, so its split maxima 0,3,4,3 prove the true binary upper bound 4. A direct binary witness has shortest word abba, proving sharpness.

value.rationale: The direct source determines the exact unrestricted extremum but its four-state extremal construction spends five distinct input symbols, while earlier work explicitly identifies fixed alphabet size as a separate regime. Determining that binary falls short by one and that ternary already restores the sharp value identifies the exact alphabet-economy boundary at the first nontrivial central-binomial case. This is structural information about the source extremum, not an arbitrary finite slice.
